description: Dual low-drift RRIO op-amp
notes: ONE op-amp part throughout the module, and THIS ROW IS WHERE THE OPA2197'S DEVICE FACTS LIVE - U-BUF and U-RESP cite it rather than repeat it. Six packages, twelve halves, ELEVEN used: pitch, mod 1-4, mod offset follower, VREFOUT follower, breath REF-zero buffer, breath gain buffer, breath summer, breath LED driver (U-REF-BUF B). ONE SPARE (U-MOD-C B); the response shaper is its own package, U-RESP, and takes neither. RRIO on +/-12V reaches ~11.9V. FROM THE BANKED SBOS737C: open-loop output impedance is SPECIFIED at 375 ohm [EC table p.8 and p.10, f = 1 MHz], with Figure 26 giving ~3.26k at 0.1Hz, 482 at 10Hz, a 375 plateau from 100Hz to 300kHz, 301 at 1MHz and ~73 at 10MHz - *** DO NOT SIZE A POLE OFF THE 10MHz VALUE, *** which is roughly 5x optimistic. Capacitive load is 1 nF max [p.1 Features, 7.3.5 p.22: 'in a unity-gain configuration, directly drives up to 1 nF of pure capacitive load'], and Figures 27/28 show that is a stable-but-RINGING limit, ~40% overshoot at unity gain - TI recommends a 10-20 ohm isolation resistor and tabulates R_ISO for 45/60 deg phase margin in Table 3 p.23. GBW 10MHz, SR 20V/us, Isc +/-65mA, IQ 1mA/amp, ~11.9V swing on +/-12V, SOIC-8 DUAL R-thJA 107.9 degC/W - note the SINGLE OPA197 is 115.8 and is a different table. PSRR is +/-1 uV/V typ and +/-3 uV/V max, i.e. 120 dB typ and 110.5 dB worst case; the '114 dB' figure is not in the document

part: 10k multiturn cermet + divider from the DAC rail (dac-rail)
description: Nulls the sensor's +0.265V pedestal at the INA828 REF pin
notes: Buffered by a half of U-OPA-PITCH - REF needs a low source impedance or it degrades CMRR one-for-one. *** RANGE 0 TO +1.0V, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE PEDESTAL IS A SPEC BAND, NOT A TYPICAL *** - the datasheet's own table gives Voff 0.152 / 0.265 / 0.378 V, so the REF needed spans 0.328-0.817V at the effective gain 2.16106. A 0.6V ceiling would leave a part at the top of its own spec UN-NULLABLE, with 1.4-5.6% of span standing at the jack; +1.0V covers the whole band with margin. The setting itself is the tracked figure breath-zero-ref; do not restate it. *** DERIVE IT FROM THE DAC RAIL (dac-rail), NOT FROM VREFOUT. *** VREFOUT is the DAC's internal reference and is DISABLED at power-on until firmware writes an enable, so taking the breath zero from it would make the analog breath path depend on a DAC register - which three documents correctly say it does not. The DAC rail is up whenever +12V is. THIS IS ALSO WHAT MAKES THE PANEL KNOBS INDEPENDENT: with REF grounded the pedestal sits upstream of the gain pot and gets multiplied. One zero authority per representation still holds - this is CALIBRATION, set once, where the panel OFFSET knob is PERFORMANCE

description: Instrumentation amp - breath receiver, senses against AGND
notes: BREATH drives IN-, AGND drives IN+, and REF is driven by TRIM-BREATH-ZERO THROUGH A BUFFER - never a bare divider, because source impedance on an in-amp REF pin degrades CMRR one-for-one. *** THE NUMBER IS 5 OHMS *** [SBOS792A section 8.1, verbatim: 'For the best performance, keep the source impedance to the REF terminal, RREF, below 5 ohm'] - RREF sits in series with one of the internal 40k difference-amp resistors and unbalances the bridge. Output runs 0V at rest to inamp-full-scale: Vout = -2.16106*(V_BREATH - V_AGND) + V_REF, with TRIM-BREATH-ZERO nulling the sensor pedestal. *** NOTE THE GAIN: 2.16106 IS THE EFFECTIVE GAIN, *** the raw G = 1 + 50k/42.2k = 2.185 times the 1M/(1M+11k) bias divider - using the raw 2.185 is the recorded way to get this wrong. The DAC ch6 zero injection that originally justified the input swap is deleted (ADR 0003). EMI: the part HAS an integrated RFI filter, -3dB at 53MHz, and EMIRR is a TABULATED characteristic rather than just a curve. *** THE WORST CASES ARE 48dB DIFFERENTIAL AT 400MHz AND 51dB COMMON-MODE AT 1.8GHz, *** and the differential and common-mode columns INVERT between 900MHz (52/98) and 1.8GHz (94/51) - so any RF-rectification argument must use those two and not the 90-plus dB numbers. TI does not claim the internal filter is sufficient on its own. See breath-receive-stage.md

description: Differential filter capacitor across the in-amp input pair
notes: THE FIXED PART OF THE SWITCHABLE DIFFERENTIAL FILTER, ALWAYS IN CIRCUIT: alone (with the two C_cm in series) it is the WIDE corner, about 10 kHz against 2 x 11 kohm, and it is 10 x C_cm, the ratio that keeps C_cm's mismatch divided down above the corner (breath-sense-link.md, 'Why C_diff is ten times C_cm'). C-DIFF-BW-1K5 and C-DIFF-BW-500 are switched in beside it by U-BW-SW. Place it AT the INA828's input pins, between the two legs, symmetric; it is the RF filter in every mode, so it must not sit behind the switch. C0G. Yageo CC0805JRNPO9BN681, LCSC C107121

description: Common-mode filter capacitors, one per leg to AGND
notes: Common-mode filter capacitors, one per leg to AGND. *** A MATCHED PAIR, NOT TWO PARTS (owner, 2026-10-03: 'Tighten cap matching'; the value is #32's, 2026-10-04): *** their mismatch converts the umbilical's common mode in proportion to frequency, so it sets the link's CMRR at the top of each bandwidth mode (breath-receive-stage/sim, cmrr-*). Each must be within 0.5 % of the pair's mean, as that sim's corners hold them. The 1 % C0G is the tightest catalogued, so: buy it from ONE REEL, measure on one LCR meter (at 100 kHz if it has it - 68 pF is 23 kohm there, where a 1 kHz bridge reads 2.3 Mohm), open-circuit compensated, and fit a pair whose two readings are within 0.5 % of their mean - by HAND, after measuring, never from the pick-and-place feeder. FIXED IN EVERY MODE, so the CMRR at a given frequency is the same whatever the toggle says. 68 pF and not more: the wide mode's corner is set by C_diff + C_cm/2 against 2 x 11 kohm, and with a larger C_cm the corner cannot reach 10 kHz with C_diff still ten times C_cm. Common-mode corner 1/(2 pi x 11 kohm x 68 pF) = 213 kHz. Yageo CC0805FRNPO9BN680, LCSC C541517; buy at least ten to pair from

description: Quad SPST analog switch: the breath bandwidth's switched capacitors
notes: Four normally-open channels on the module's +/-12 V (VDD-VSS 24 V of its 10-34 V), GND on AGND_MOD. Each switched C_diff is switched AT BOTH ENDS, one channel per leg, so the switch's own capacitance (CD(OFF) 2.4 pF typ, CD(ON) 4.2 pF typ [ds TMUX6112-ti-scds383f.pdf p.7]) loads the two legs alike: it is common-mode capacitance, and its channel-to-channel match, which the datasheet does not give, is part of the link's CMRR (breath-receive-stage/sim). LAY THE TWO LEGS OUT AS MIRROR IMAGES. RON 120 ohm typ is in series with a switched capacitor and moves no corner by more than 0.6 % (sim). Off leakage 0.02 nA max at 25 C into 11 kohm is 0.2 uV. Beside the INA828 on module-main. LCSC C2673384

notes: ON-ON-ON on a double-pole base (owner, 2026-10-04: 'Panel 3-way toggle', '500 Hz / 1.5 kHz / wide'; left-right like SW-POWER: 'full left being 500 full right being wide is the intuitive placement because it matches the on off of the power switch'). MOUNT IT AS SW-POWER IS, D-FLAT ON THE LEFT: lever right is NKK's Down (makes 2-3, 5-6), centre is Center (2-3, 5-4), lever left is Up (2-1, 5-4) [ds NKK-SERIES-M-TOGGLE.pdf p.5]. The panel has no position words: buzz it on arrival, lever left pad 1 to pads 2 and 3, centre pad 1 to pad 2 only, right neither. It carries DC only (about 0.8 mA a line): the analog pair never leaves the board. *** CONTACT MATERIAL G, GOLD - NEVER W ***, as SW-POWER: gold's applicable range starts at 0.1 mA [ds p.1]. Same series, bushing and panel hole as SW-POWER (the tracked figure panel-toggle-hole), one front nut, but a DOUBLE-POLE BODY: 12.7mm across (SW-POWER 7.9), 9.4mm behind the bushing, lug rows 4.8mm apart [ds p.11].
